evidence_set.scope: Three primary records already cited by Open Enzyme for quercetin, curcumin, and EGCG ABCG2/BCRP interaction signals; not a literature census
evidence_set.selection_rule: One named primary record per compound, chosen only to test whether that cited record supports a quantitative intestinal urate-transport conclusion.

records.assay_context: Functional BCRP assays used drug substrates in non-intestinal cell systems.

source.citation: Cooray et al. Biochem Biophys Res Commun. 2004.

records.assay_context: A cynomolgus-monkey intestinal drug-interaction study used sulfasalazine and rosuvastatin as BCRP probe substrates.

source.citation: Karibe et al. Drug Metab Dispos. 2018.

records.assay_context: After EGCG exposure, a tamoxifen-resistant MCF-7 mitoxantrone assay showed reduced BCRP activity without changed BCRP mRNA or protein.
